title: AI Operators for Insurance: Transforming Customer Experience
summary: The Mission Control Engine For Reliable AI Agents
body_text: The insurance industry is on the brink of a seismic shift. Customers demand faster, more personalised services, but outdated systems and rising expectations create significant hurdles. Insurers are left asking: how can we keep up without compromising compliance, operational efficiency, or customer trust? For the last 2 years, AI agents were heralded as the solution—but widespread adoption never came. Why? Because most AI agents couldn't take action. They could answer questions but failed to resolve real issues. They were often limited to scripted dialogues or rigid integrations, unable to handle the complexity of live insurance operations. AI Operators are a new breed. Purpose-built to get things done, they go beyond conversation. They observe real human agents, learn workflows, and execute actions without engineering effort or API dependencies. Consider this scenario: a customer contacts support late at night, struggling to update payment details for a policy renewal. A traditional chatbot might suggest contacting support during office hours, causing frustration. In contrast, an AI Operator instantly updates the payment information, confirms renewal status, and provides immediate reassurance—showcasing true problem-solving capabilities. In this guide, we explore how AI Operators are finally delivering on the promise of AI in insurance. Challenges Facing the Insurance Industry The insurance sector faces several hurdles that directly impact customer satisfaction, operational performance, and scalability. If any of these sound familiar, you're not alone: Meeting Customer Expectations with Personalisation Today's customers expect service as intuitive and personalised as what they receive in industries like tech or retail. Insurers, however, often struggle with outdated systems and siloed data. This creates missed opportunities for proactive engagement, efficient issue resolution, and tailored recommendations. Personalised service is no longer a luxury—it's a necessity for building trust and loyalty. Imagine a policyholder receiving tailored policy recommendations or renewal reminders based on their specific needs—this level of service fosters long-term loyalty and satisfaction. Embracing Digital Transformation Digital-first customers demand instant service and seamless self-service options. Yet, legacy systems frequently fail to deliver the cohesive experiences customers expect. The result? Frustration, churn, and lost opportunities. Insurers without a unified digital strategy risk falling behind. For example, when a customer attempts to update their policy online but encounters glitches or incomplete options, it leaves a negative impression that could lead them to explore competitors. Implementing robust digital interfaces backed by AI ensures smooth, reliable experiences. Balancing Efficiency with Regulatory Compliance Operating within strict data privacy and regulatory frameworks like GDPR and HIPAA adds complexity. Meanwhile, rising cyber threats and fraud further increase the stakes. Balancing operational efficiency with compliance and robust cybersecurity measures is a must for insurers to stay competitive and trusted. AI solutions with embedded compliance capabilities can proactively flag risks and ensure all processes align with regulatory standards, minimising legal and reputational risks. These challenges highlight the urgent need for intelligent, scalable solutions that can adapt to the evolving demands of the industry. How AI Operators Are Transforming Insurance AI Operators are at the forefront of innovation in insurance, combining advanced machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and automation. Unlike legacy AI agents, they don't stop at conversation. They take action. 1. Enhanced Customer Engagement AI Operators powered by NLP interpret and respond to customer inquiries with precision, enhancing satisfaction and reducing miscommunication. They handle nuanced questions, such as clarifying policy exclusions or explaining premium calculations, with speed and clarity. Multilingual capabilities allow insurers to serve diverse customer bases effectively and inclusively, fostering trust across global markets. AI Operators also ensure omnichannel consistency, allowing customers to begin queries on one platform and continue seamlessly on another, reducing friction and improving the overall experience. Use Case: First Notice of Loss (FNOL) Picture this: a customer involved in a minor accident uses their insurer's app to file a claim. An AI Operator immediately steps in, guiding the user through uploading photos of the damage and providing real-time updates on the claim's status. The customer feels reassured and supported at a stressful moment—a win for both the customer and the insurer. 2. Effortless Deployment and Human-Level Execution AI Operators are designed to be deployed quickly with no-code implementation. They mimic human agents by learning from real interactions and applying the same logic and workflows—without requiring backend integrations or development support. This makes them highly practical and scalable, especially for insurers looking to modernise operations without a heavy lift. Use Case: Fast Deployment with Human-Like Interaction Imagine launching an AI Operator that instantly slots into your claims team, replicating how your top-performing agent processes water damage claims—reviewing receipts, validating coverage, and initiating payouts—without a single line of code or system integration. 3. Operational Efficiency By automating repetitive tasks such as routine policy checks, claims processing, or identity verification (ID&V), AI Operators save time and resources. For example, they can validate documentation instantly, reducing processing times from days to minutes. This enables human teams to focus on higher-value tasks like resolving complex claims or improving customer relationships. Use Case: Claims Processing Imagine a policyholder submitting a claim for water damage. An AI Operator reviews the uploaded receipts, verifies them against policy terms, and processes the payout—all within hours, not weeks. The efficiency not only delights the customer but also reduces operational costs significantly. 4. Scalable, Cost-Effective Solutions AI Operators handle increasing customer volumes effortlessly, maintaining service quality even during demand surges, such as natural disasters or renewal periods. By automating call centre operations, reducing manual errors, and preventing fraud-related losses, they help insurers significantly cut operational costs while providing flexibility to scale services as needed. Use Case: Proactive Renewals & Upselling Consider a scenario where a customer's home insurance policy is about to expire. An AI Operator analyses their current coverage, suggests additional options like flood insurance based on local risk data, and even schedules the renewal with a single click. The customer appreciates the proactive approach, and the insurer secures an upsell. 5. Compliance and Security AI platforms are designed with built-in compliance tools to adhere to stringent regulatory requirements such as GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA, and SOC 2. Robust security measures, including encryption and audit trails, ensure sensitive customer data remains protected while providing full transparency for regulatory bodies. Self-healing capabilities ensure that Operators stay updated with the latest compliance requirements, minimising legal risks and maintaining trust. Use Case: Policy Management Picture an AI Operator monitoring regulatory changes and automatically updating policy language to ensure compliance. For instance, after a new GDPR amendment, the AI ensures that all documents meet the latest requirements, saving the insurer time and mitigating risk. All these features are possible with Eloquent AI's advanced technologies, purpose-built to tackle the unique challenges of the insurance industry. Action-Oriented Tool Calling: Operators can take real steps like processing claims, updating policies, or initiating refunds—without API dependencies. Precision Through RAG Technology: Retrieval-Augmented Generation allows Operators to pull relevant information directly from your documentation and apply it in context. Tailored Industry Expertise: Our models are trained specifically on insurance workflows, terminology, and regulatory frameworks, enabling Operators to deliver results with confidence. A Step-by-Step Journey to AI Integration Implementing AI Operators in insurance is not just a technical project—it's a journey that transforms how insurers operate. Picture this: a mid-sized insurance company facing mounting customer inquiries and strained resources decides to introduce AI Operators into their operations. They don't jump into the deep end but instead follow a step-by-step strategy to ensure success: Map the Customer Journey The company analyses the end-to-end customer experience to pinpoint areas where AI Operators can deliver the greatest impact. For example, they identify that automating the first notice of loss (FNOL) process can drastically improve claims reporting. Build a Pilot Program Rather than rolling out AI across all departments, the company tests it in a controlled environment, such as claims processing. This allows them to gather insights, address challenges, and refine the solution before scaling. Imagine beginning with automating claims status updates—a repetitive but high-volume task that bogs down call centres. By implementing an AI Operator, the company quickly reduces wait times for customers while freeing up human agents to handle more complex cases. This initial win builds momentum and confidence within the team, showcasing how AI can deliver measurable results. Empower Your Team The company prioritises training sessions to demystify AI's role, emphasising that AI Operators are there to enhance—not replace—human expertise. Employees shift their focus to high-value tasks, like providing personalised policy advice or resolving emotionally sensitive claims, allowing them to build stronger relationships with policyholders. Focus on Compliance and Security As the company integrates AI, they ensure that robust data protection measures and regulatory adherence are embedded into the system. This builds trust with both regulators and policyholders. Continuously Optimise and Scale Strategically As the AI Operators go live, the company monitors performance metrics and gathers customer feedback. When the Operators encounter questions they can't fully resolve, these gaps are logged and used to refine their knowledge base. Over time, the Operators evolve to handle an even broader range of inquiries. With demonstrated success, the company gradually scales AI to other business areas. This step-by-step approach ensures that AI Operators are not just implemented but integrated effectively into the company's operations, delivering ongoing value and transforming the customer experience. A Step-by-Step Journey to AI Integration The Future of Insurance with AI Operators AI Operators are not just tools—they're transformative enablers reshaping the insurance industry. By leveraging AI Operators, insurers can revolutionise customer engagement, operations, and transparency. Proactive customer engagement becomes possible as AI Operators predict customer needs and provide tailored solutions even before customers ask. For instance, an AI Operator might alert a policyholder about additional coverage options as their circumstances evolve. Operations become highly scalable, allowing insurers to handle demand surges during natural disasters or renewal periods without compromising service quality. AI Operators ensure that no customer inquiry goes unanswered, even during peak times. Moreover, enhanced transparency through explainable AI fosters clarity in decision-making, building trust with both customers and regulators. This clarity proves especially critical in sensitive situations, such as claim denials or policy cancellations. Don't Wait to Lead the Future Eloquent AI empowers insurers to embrace transformation and deliver measurable results. From reducing operational costs to enhancing customer satisfaction and ensuring compliance, our solutions are built to help you succeed. Don't wait to fall behind. Book a demo today and discover how Eloquent AI can revolutionise your insurance operations.

title: 90791 CPT Code: Psychiatric Diagnostic Evaluation
summary: The 90791 CPT code covers psychiatric diagnostic evaluation without medical services. It is an untimed code, and 90792 applies when you prescribe.
body_text: The 90791 CPT code covers a psychiatric diagnostic evaluation without medical services. It is the intake code: the comprehensive initial assessment where a clinician takes the history, performs a mental status exam, establishes a diagnosis and sets a treatment direction. Two things about it surprise people. It is not a timed code , unlike the psychotherapy codes it sits next to. And if the clinician prescribes or manages medication during that evaluation, the correct code is 90792, not 90791. Below: what the code covers, why time thresholds do not apply, how 90791 differs from 90792 and from 90837, how often payers let you bill it, what can share the claim, telehealth, and the documentation a 90791 note needs to survive review. What the 90791 CPT Code Covers The official descriptor is "psychiatric diagnostic evaluation" . The companion code 90792 is "psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services". The distinction between them is the entire reason miscoding this pair is one of the most common errors in psychiatric billing. A 90791 evaluation generally includes a full biopsychosocial history, a mental status examination, a risk assessment, a diagnosis, and a recommended treatment plan. It is billable by psychologists, licensed clinical social workers, licensed professional counselors, marriage and family therapists and other qualified non-prescribing clinicians, subject to scope of practice and payer credentialing. 90791 Is Not a Timed Code There is no minute threshold for 90791. What qualifies the encounter is completing and documenting a full evaluation, not hitting a clock target. Most evaluations run somewhere between 45 and 90 minutes, but that range is a description of practice, not a billing requirement. This is where clinicians coming from the psychotherapy codes get tripped up. 90837 , 90834 and 90832 are strictly time-defined. 90791 is not. CMS lists the time-based psychotherapy services as 90832 through 90838 and requires start and stop times for those codes specifically; 90791 is absent from that list, which is the clearest confirmation that it is untimed. The practical consequence: do not withhold a 90791 because the session ran short, and do not assume a long evaluation earns anything extra. Document the completeness of the assessment instead of its duration. 30% MORE BOOKINGS mdhub, powering clinics with AI Built for mental health BOOK A FREE DEMO → 90791 vs 90792: The Prescriber Line Use 90791 when no medical services are provided, and 90792 when they are. Medical services means a medical assessment component such as a physical examination, ordering or interpreting labs, or prescribing and managing medication. 90791 90792 Descriptor Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services Who reports it Non-prescribing clinicians: psychologists, LCSWs, LPCs, MFTs Prescribers: psychiatrists, and NPs or PAs with prescribing authority Includes medication management No Yes Timed No No One detail worth knowing for prescriber-led intakes: CMS states that a physician or non-physician practitioner may use either 90792 or an evaluation and management code for the encounter. The choice is between those two, not 90791 plus an E/M code on top. 90791 vs 90837: An Intake Is Not a Therapy Session These two get compared constantly because both describe a long first appointment, but they are different services. 90791 is a diagnostic assessment: the output is a diagnosis and a plan. 90837 is treatment: the output is a therapeutic intervention delivered for 53 minutes or more. A first appointment is normally the evaluation, so it bills as 90791. Once treatment begins, subsequent sessions bill as psychotherapy under the time-based codes. Our guide to psychiatric billing covers how the psychotherapy and evaluation and management components fit together after intake. How Often You Can Bill 90791 This is payer policy, not a CPT rule, and it is a leading cause of denials. Most plans cover a psychiatric diagnostic evaluation once per episode of care, with common guidance falling somewhere in the range of every six to twelve months for the same patient and provider. What that means in practice: a returning patient after a long gap may legitimately warrant a new evaluation, and a patient transferring between clinicians inside the same organization may not. Because the limits differ by plan, the reliable move is to check the specific payer's medical policy before the appointment rather than after the denial. Repeat and duplicate intakes are a routine denial category, and they are avoidable at the scheduling step. What Else Can Go on the Claim Interactive complexity (90785) can be reported with 90791 and 90792. The CMS billing and coding article for psychiatric diagnostic evaluation and psychotherapy services lists the add-on as used in conjunction with the diagnostic evaluation codes, alongside the psychotherapy codes. It applies when specific communication factors complicate delivery, such as a language barrier, caregiver interference, or a mandatory reporting discussion. CMS also notes that if a patient is unable to communicate by any means, 90785 should not be billed. Psychotherapy is a different story. Payers and claim edits generally will not accept a psychotherapy code on the same day as a psychiatric diagnostic evaluation from the same provider for the same patient, because the evaluation is treated as the service of record for that encounter. Confirm the specific rule with each payer before building it into a workflow, since the enforcement mechanism varies. Can You Bill 90791 for Telehealth? Generally yes. 90791 is commonly delivered and reimbursed by telehealth, reported with the telehealth modifier and place-of-service code the payer requires. Telehealth requirements have been revised repeatedly since 2020 and differ between Medicare and commercial plans, so verify the current expectation with each payer rather than carrying forward last year's configuration, and document the session modality in the note. What Payers Check on a 90791 Note Because the code is untimed, the note carries the entire burden of proving the service. Six elements make a 90791 defensible. Presenting problem and history. The biopsychosocial context that prompted the evaluation. Mental status examination. Its absence is one of the most reliable ways to lose a 90791 on review. Risk assessment. Suicidality, self-harm and safety, documented explicitly rather than implied. A diagnosis with its ICD-10 code. An evaluation that establishes no diagnosis invites a question about what the service accomplished. Treatment recommendation. The plan the evaluation produced, including the modality and cadence proposed. Modality and date of service details, including telehealth specifics where they apply. Note format matters as much as content. A structured note where a reviewer can find the mental status exam and the risk assessment without hunting is easier to defend than a narrative that contains the same information scattered through prose. 30% MORE BOOKINGS mdhub, powering clinics with AI Built for mental health BOOK A FREE DEMO → What a Denied 90791 Costs, and How to Look Up What It Pays There is no single national figure worth quoting, and any article that gives you one is guessing at your contract. Medicare rates for 90791 are published in the CMS Physician Fee Schedule lookup and vary by locality. Commercial rates are set by your contract, so pull your own fee schedule. The cost that matters is not the line item. A denied intake sits at the front of the treatment relationship, so the rework lands while the patient is still being scheduled: staff time to identify the denial, correct and resubmit, and the delay before the claim clears. Handling this upstream is what good behavioral health billing looks like, because a denial at intake also delays every downstream claim for that episode. Where mdhub Fits Two parts of the intake problem are operational rather than clinical, and both sit outside the clinical hour. The first is everything before the evaluation: verifying coverage, confirming the payer's frequency policy for a diagnostic evaluation, and getting the patient booked with the right clinician. Sarah, the mdhub AI Admissions Coordinator, handles that admissions path, which is where a repeat-intake denial gets prevented rather than appealed. The second is the note. Emma, the mdhub AI Clinical Assistant, drafts clinical documentation and handles CPT coding, with a quality layer that checks notes against payer expectations, so an intake note reaches the biller with its mental status exam, risk assessment and diagnosis in place. On the claim side, Eric, the mdhub AI Billing Specialist, handles submission and denials. Clinics using mdhub save 2+ hours per clinician per day and see up to 50% lower operational costs . mdhub empowers clinicians rather than replacing their judgment. Emma drafts, the clinician reviews and signs. The assessment, the diagnosis and the risk determination stay with the person who conducted the evaluation. Talkiatry chose mdhub's AI clinical documentation tool to reduce the administrative load on its clinicians. For more on how the documentation side works, see our approach to AI clinical documentation for behavioral health , and what mental health billing software built for behavioral health actually does. Streamline Your Practice 90791 is a simple code with an unforgiving note. Because nothing about the time defends it, the assessment has to be visible on the page: history, mental status, risk, diagnosis, plan. Get that consistently and the intake claim stops being a recurring rework item. To see how this runs inside a live practice, book a demo with the mdhub team . What is the difference between CPT 90791 and 90792? 90791 is a psychiatric diagnostic evaluation without medical services. 90792 is the same evaluation with medical services, meaning a medical component such as a physical examination, ordering labs, or prescribing and managing medication, so it requires a clinician with prescribing authority. If medication is prescribed or managed during the intake, 90792 applies rather than 90791. CMS also states that a physician or non-physician practitioner may use either 90792 or an evaluation and management code for the encounter, so the choice for a prescriber is between those two rather than adding an E/M code to 90791. Miscoding this pair is one of the most common psychiatric billing errors. Is there a time requirement for CPT 90791? No. 90791 is an untimed code, which sets it apart from the psychotherapy codes next to it. CMS identifies 90832 through 90838 as the time-based psychotherapy services and requires start and stop times for those; 90791 is not in that group. What qualifies the encounter is a complete, documented evaluation rather than a minute threshold. Most evaluations run roughly 45 to 90 minutes, but that is a description of typical practice and not a billing requirement, so a thorough shorter evaluation is still billable and a longer one does not earn an additional line. How often can 90791 be billed for the same patient? This is payer policy rather than a CPT rule. Most plans cover a diagnostic evaluation once per episode of care, and guidance commonly lands in the range of every six to twelve months for the same patient and provider. A returning patient after a long absence may warrant a new evaluation; a patient moving between clinicians within one organization often does not. Because the limits genuinely differ between plans, check the payer's medical policy before the appointment. Repeat or duplicate intakes are a routine denial category and the cheapest place to catch one is at scheduling. Can 90791 be billed on the same day as psychotherapy? Generally no. Payers and automated claim edits typically reject a psychotherapy code billed on the same day as a psychiatric diagnostic evaluation by the same provider for the same patient, because the evaluation is treated as the service of record for that encounter. Interactive complexity is the exception worth knowing: CMS lists 90785 as reportable in conjunction with 90791 and 90792. Because enforcement varies by payer and edit set, confirm the specific pairing rule with each plan before you build it into a scheduling or billing workflow.

title: HitPay vs Airwallex Singapore — Which Platform Fits Your Business?
summary: HitPay handles local payment acceptance. Airwallex handles global treasury. Here’s which platform fits your Singapore business model.
body_text: Quick Answer: HitPay and Airwallex are not direct competitors — they serve different business models. HitPay is built for local payment acceptance: PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Atome, and cards, with no monthly fee and next business day SGD payouts. Airwallex is built for global treasury: multi-currency accounts, FX transfers, and corporate spend management. A Singapore café or online retailer needs HitPay. A Singapore company paying overseas contractors or managing multi-currency cash flow needs Airwallex. Both hold MAS licences; the decision comes down to what your business actually does. Singapore’s digital payments market is one of the most competitive in Southeast Asia, with consumers regularly switching between PayNow, GrabPay, and card payments at checkout. For a merchant in Tiong Bahru or an online seller based in Bugis, choosing the wrong payment platform means missing transactions — not just paying higher fees. HitPay and Airwallex are both well-known names in Singapore fintech, but they solve different problems. Understanding that distinction is the first step to making the right choice. What does each platform actually do? HitPay is a payment gateway and POS platform built for SMBs across Singapore and Southeast Asia. It handles payment acceptance — online, in-person, and via payment links — with 50+ payment methods including all major local options. Airwallex positions itself as an intelligent financial platform for global businesses. Its core products are multi-currency business accounts, global FX transfers, corporate cards, and expense management. Payment acceptance (checkout, payment links) is available but secondary to its treasury and spend management offering. The distinction matters. A café in Orchard Road needs PayNow QR, GrabPay, and a card terminal. A software company paying overseas contractors needs multi-currency accounts and low FX rates. These are different tools. What payment methods does each platform support in Singapore? This is where the gap is most visible. HitPay — Singapore payment methods: - PayNow QR - GrabPay - ShopeePay - Atome (BNPL) - ShopBack Pay (BNPL) - GrabPay PayLater (BNPL) - Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Apple Pay, Google Pay - Cross-border: WeChatPay (China), UPI (India), QRIS (Indonesia), DuitNow (Malaysia), PromptPay & TrueMoney & Rabbit LINE Pay (Thailand), QR Ph (Philippines), KakaoPay/PayCo/LINE Pay (South Korea) Airwallex — Singapore payment methods: - Cards (Visa, Mastercard) - 160+ local payment methods globally, but local SGD wallet coverage (GrabPay, ShopeePay, PayNow) is not confirmed as a core product offering For merchants whose customers pay with GrabPay or PayNow — which covers the majority of retail transactions in Singapore — HitPay’s breadth is a clear operational advantage. As covered in our guide to online payment methods in Singapore , local e-wallets and instant bank transfers now account for a significant share of consumer spend. How do fees and pricing compare? Feature HitPay Airwallex Monthly fee None Explore: Free; Grow: SGD ~$79/month; Accelerate: from $399/month Setup fee None None Pricing model Per-transaction only Subscription + per-transaction for FX, payments, cards Card transaction rate See hitpayapp.com/pricing Per-transaction fees apply Local e-wallet acceptance PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Atome, ShopBack Pay PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Atome, ShopBack Pay BNPL Atome, ShopBack Pay, GrabPay PayLater Atome, ShopBack Pay Multi-currency accounts Not core product Yes — key differentiator Corporate cards Not offered Yes — multi-currency cards Expense management Not offered Yes For a merchant processing $30,000 SGD per month with no need for corporate cards or FX accounts, HitPay’s zero monthly fee structure results in lower fixed costs. Airwallex’s subscription tiers make more sense for businesses that actively use the FX and spend management features to offset the monthly cost. How fast do payouts arrive? HitPay settles domestic SGD transactions on the next business day. Cross-border payments (e.g., a Chinese tourist paying via WeChatPay) settle next business day in SGD. This is a predictable cash flow cycle for retailers and online sellers. Airwallex’s payout speed depends on the product being used. For payment acceptance, settlement timelines are not uniformly published for SGD domestic transactions at the SMB level. For a retail operator managing payroll or inventory reorders, next business day SGD payouts from HitPay reduce working capital pressure. Which platform is right for which business? HitPay Best for: Singapore SMBs — retailers, F&B operators, online sellers, service providers — that need to accept PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, BNPL, and cards with zero monthly fees and next business day SGD payouts, without the complexity of a financial platform. Airwallex Best for: Singapore businesses that need multi-currency global accounts, interbank-rate FX transfers, and corporate expense management — particularly those paying international suppliers or managing treasury across multiple currencies. Both platforms operate in a regulated environment. Payment service providers in Singapore are licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) under the Payment Services Act. HitPay holds licence PS20200643. Merchants should verify any provider’s MAS licence status before onboarding. For businesses evaluating cross-border payment acceptance specifically — accepting wallets from Thai, Indonesian, Indian, or Chinese visitors — HitPay’s cross-border method coverage is worth reviewing in detail. A boutique in Orchard Road accepting QRIS from Indonesian tourists or UPI from Indian visitors gains incremental revenue without any currency exchange friction at the point of sale. Our breakdown of B2B multi-currency payments in Singapore covers how cross-border acceptance and cross-border payments serve different operational needs. Practical takeaway The HitPay vs Airwallex decision is less about which platform is better and more about which problem a business is actually solving. Airwallex is a financial infrastructure platform; HitPay is a payment acceptance platform. Most Singapore retailers, F&B operators, and online sellers need the latter — with local e-wallet coverage, no monthly fees, and reliable next business day payouts. Businesses that have significant international treasury needs or multi-currency expense management requirements will find Airwallex’s product set more relevant. HitPay is free to sign up and approvals take 1–3 business days. Visit hitpayapp.com/pricing for current transaction rates. Frequently Asked Questions Is HitPay or Airwallex better for a small retail business in Singapore? HitPay is the stronger choice for most Singapore retail businesses. It supports PayNow, GrabPay, ShopeePay, Atome, ShopBack Pay, and cards with zero monthly fees and next business day SGD payouts. Airwallex is primarily a financial platform focused on global accounts and FX — not optimised for local retail payment acceptance. Does Airwallex support PayNow and GrabPay in Singapore? Airwallex’s primary product offering in Singapore centres on multi-currency accounts, corporate cards, and FX transfers. Airwallex supports PayNow, GrabPay, and ShopeePay in Singapore. HitPay’s primary advantages are zero monthly fees (vs SGD 79+/month for Airwallex), broader cross-border QR coverage (UPI, QRIS, PromptPay, DuitNow, Korean wallets), and an onboarding process built for SMBs. Does HitPay charge a monthly fee in Singapore? HitPay charges no monthly fee and no setup fee. Merchants pay per transaction only. Card transaction rates are published at hitpayapp.com/pricing. This structure makes HitPay cost-effective for SMBs at any volume level. How long does HitPay take to pay out funds in Singapore? HitPay settles domestic SGD transactions on the next business day. Cross-border payment methods — such as WeChatPay, UPI, or QRIS — settle at next business day in SGD. Payouts are made directly to the merchant’s Singapore bank account. Is HitPay regulated in Singapore? Yes. HitPay is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) under the Payment Services Act, with licence number PS20200643. MAS maintains a public register of licensed payment service providers that merchants can consult to verify any provider’s regulatory status. When should a Singapore business choose Airwallex over HitPay? Airwallex is the better fit when a business primarily needs multi-currency global accounts, interbank-rate FX transfers, or corporate expense management across multiple currencies — rather than local payment acceptance. A Singapore SaaS company paying overseas contractors in USD, GBP, and EUR would benefit more from Airwallex’s treasury tools than from HitPay’s retail checkout capabilities. What cross-border payment methods can Singapore merchants accept through HitPay? HitPay enables Singapore merchants to accept payments from international visitors using their home-country apps, including WeChatPay (China), UPI (India), QRIS (Indonesia), DuitNow (Malaysia), PromptPay, TrueMoney, and Rabbit LINE Pay (Thailand), QR Ph (Philippines), and KakaoPay, PayCo, and LINE Pay (South Korea). No currency exchange is needed at the point of sale. Cross-border transactions settle at next business day in SGD.

title: Federal Realty Announces Proposed Private Placement of $400 Million of Exchangeable Senior Notes
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Federal Realty Investment Trust's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: NORTH BETHESDA, Md. , Aug. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Federal Realty Investment Trust (NYSE: FRT) ("Federal Realty") announced today that its operating partnership, Federal Realty OP LP (the "Partnership"), launched an offering (the "Offering"), subject to market conditions and other factors, of $400 million aggregate principal amount of exchangeable senior notes due 2031 (the "notes") in a private placement to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). The Partnership also intends to grant the initial purchasers of the notes an option to purchase, during a 13-day period beginning on, and including, the first date on which the notes are issued, up to an additional $60.0 million aggregate principal amount of notes. The notes will be the Partnership's senior unsecured obligations and will accrue interest payable semi-annually in arrears. Subject to certain conditions, the notes will be exchangeable for cash up to the principal amount of the notes exchanged and, in respect of the remainder of the exchange value, if any, in excess thereof, cash or common shares of beneficial interest, par value $.01 per share, of Federal Realty ("common shares"), or a combination thereof, at the election of the Partnership. The interest rate, exchange rate and other terms of the notes will be determined at the time of pricing of the Offering. The Partnership intends to use the net proceeds from the Offering to pay the cost of the capped call transactions described below, for the repayment of indebtedness and for general corporate purposes. Pending such use, the net proceeds may be invested in short-term, income-producing investments or the Partnership may use the net proceeds to temporarily repay current and/or future amounts outstanding under its revolving credit facility. If the initial purchasers of the notes exercise their option to purchase additional notes, the Partnership expects to use a portion of the net proceeds from the sale of the additional notes to enter into additional capped call transactions with the option counterparties and the remaining net proceeds for the purposes described above. In connection with the pricing of the notes, Federal Realty and the Partnership expect to enter into privately negotiated capped call transactions relating to the notes with one or more of the initial purchasers of the notes or their respective affiliates and/or other financial institutions (the "option counterparties"). The capped call transactions will cover, subject to customary adjustments, the number of Federal Realty's common shares that will initially underlie the notes. The capped call transactions are expected generally to reduce the potential dilution to Federal Realty's common shares upon exchange of any notes and/or offset any cash payments the Partnership is required to make in excess of the principal amount of exchanged notes, as the case may be, with such reduction and/or offset subject to a cap. In connection with establishing their initial hedges of the capped call transactions, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates may enter into various derivative transactions with respect to Federal Realty's common shares and/or purchase Federal Realty's common shares or other securities of Federal Realty in secondary market transactions concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes, including with or from, as the case may be, certain investors in the notes. This activity could increase (or reduce the size of any decrease in) the market price of Federal Realty's common shares or the notes at that time. In addition, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates may modify or unwind their hedge positions by entering into or unwinding various derivatives with respect to Federal Realty's common shares and/or purchasing or selling Federal Realty's common shares or other securities of Federal Realty or the Partnership in secondary market transactions following the pricing of the notes and prior to the maturity of the notes (and are likely to do so following any fundamental change repurchase, redemption or early exchange of the notes and during the 40 trading day period beginning on the 41st scheduled trading day prior to the maturity date of the notes, or, to the extent the Partnership exercises the relevant election under the capped call transactions, following any other repurchase of the notes). This activity could also cause, reduce the extent of or avoid an increase or a decrease in the market price of Federal Realty's common shares or the notes, which could affect a noteholder's ability to exchange the notes, and, to the extent the activity occurs following exchange or during any observation period related to an exchange of notes, it could affect the number of common shares, if any, and value of the consideration that noteholders will receive upon exchange of the notes. Neither the notes nor the common shares issuable upon exchange of the notes have been registered under the Securities Act or any state securities laws, and unless so registered, may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the registration requirements of the Securities Act and other applicable securities laws. Accordingly, the notes are being offered and sold only to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers (as defined in Rule 144A under the Securities Act). This press release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy, nor shall there be any offer or sale of, the notes in any jurisdiction in which the offer, solicitation or sale of the notes would be unlawful prior to the registration or qualification thereof under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction. Safe Harbor Statement This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. These statements may be identified by use of terms such as "propose," "will," "expect," "shall," and similar terms or the negative of such terms, and include, without limitation, statements regarding the expected timing, size, and completion of the proposed Offering, the grant to the initial purchasers of the option to purchase additional notes, the expected use of the net proceeds of the Offering, and other information that is not historical information. Actual results or developments may differ materially from those projected or implied in these forward-looking statements. Factors that may cause such a difference include risks and uncertainties related to completion of the Offering on the anticipated terms or at all, market conditions, and the satisfaction of customary closing conditions related to the Offering. More information about the risks and uncertainties faced by Federal Realty and the Partnership is contained in the section captioned "Risk Factors" in Federal Realty's and the Partnership's Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") filings, including their Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, as well as subsequent SEC filings. The forward-looking statements contained in this release are as of the date of this release, and, except as required by law, neither Federal Realty nor the Partnership undertakes any obligation to update any such statements, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise. About Federal Realty Federal Realty is a recognized leader in the ownership, operation and redevelopment of high-quality retail-based properties located primarily in major coastal markets and select underserved regions with strong economic and demographic fundamentals. Founded in 1962, Federal Realty's mission is to deliver long-term, sustainable growth through investing in communities where retail demand exceeds supply. This includes a portfolio of open-air shopping centers and mixed-use destinations—such as Santana Row, Pike & Rose, and Assembly Row—which together reflect the company's ability to create distinctive, high-performing environments that serve as vibrant destinations for their communities. Federal Realty's 103 properties include approximately 3,700 tenants in 28.8 million commercial square feet, and approximately 2,700 residential units. Federal Realty has increased its quarterly dividends per common share for 59 consecutive years on an annualized basis, the longest record in the REIT industry. Federal Realty is an S&P 500 index member and its shares are traded on the NYSE under the symbol FRT. title: The Hidden Risks of Child Interpreters in Care
summary: Using family members as medical interpreters doubles error rates and risks Section 1557 violations. See what the law requires and what works better. August 2026
body_text: A 13-year-old stands at the foot of his mother's exam table, relaying the physician's instructions. He gets through the drug name. He cannot find the words for the dosing warning and skips it. If something goes wrong at home, that gap belongs to you. Good intentions do not cancel out clinical risk. TLDR: Ad hoc interpreters produce clinically consequential errors 22% of the time, nearly double the 12% rate for professional interpreters. Child interpreters carry even greater risk: one AHRQ-reviewed case found 84% of a child's errors had potential clinical consequences. Patients actively withhold sensitive information, including domestic violence and mental health symptoms, when a family member holds the conversation. Section 1557's 2024 rule bars covered entities from using minor children to interpret except during genuine emergencies with imminent safety threats. Opalite Health provides AI medical interpretation across 150-plus languages for routine encounters, with escalation pathways to qualified human interpreters for high-stakes situations. Why family members end up as interpreters in clinical settings It rarely starts as a decision. A patient arrives, the clinic is busy, and the certified interpreter line has a wait. Someone in the room already speaks both languages, usually a spouse, an adult child, or a teenager pulled from a waiting room chair. The visit moves forward. Several pressures push toward this workaround: Interpreter connection delays during peak hours After-hours and weekend gaps in coverage Thin availability for rare languages and dialects Patient comfort with a trusted relative in the room The quiet assumption that any bilingual person can interpret the job Providers and families both mean well. Good intentions, though, do not cancel out clinical risk. The accuracy problem with untrained interpreters Intuition says an untrained bilingual relative will make more mistakes. The literature puts a number on it. In a cross-sectional study of pediatric emergency department encounters, ad hoc interpreters produced errors with potential clinical consequences 22% of the time, compared with 12% for professional medical interpreter services , across 1,884 recorded errors . The errors fall into recognizable patterns: Omission: leaving out part of what was said, the most common error type False fluency: inventing words or phrases that were never spoken Substitution: swapping in a different word, symptom, or dose Editorialization: inserting the interpreter's own opinion or judgment Each one changes the clinical record. A dropped symptom or an altered dose is a safety event waiting to happen. When the interpreter is a child Consider one documented case. When an 11-year-old sibling interpreted during a pediatric encounter, 84% of the 58 errors she committed carried potential clinical consequences, a rate far above that of adult ad hoc interpreters, according to a case reviewed by AHRQ . A child in that seat is set up to struggle: Bilingual skills are still developing, so vocabulary runs short in both languages Medical terms like "seizure" or "milligrams" have never been part of their world Sensitive topics get skipped out of embarrassment or protectiveness Impartiality is impossible when the patient is their own parent None of this reflects a failing on the child's part. They are carrying a job no one should hand them. The psychological toll on young language brokers The accuracy risk is only half the harm. The other half lands on the child. Clinicians call this parentification: a child absorbing adult responsibilities well beyond what is developmentally appropriate. A 2025 case report described "Interpreter Child Syndrome" in a nine-year-old refugee girl who developed anxiety, somatic symptoms, and academic decline after averaging 10 to 15 hours a week interpreting for her mother, including sensitive gynecological and mental health appointments, as documented in a published case report . Healthcare content makes the role reversal worse. When the words a child must relay are frightening or intimate, they carry meaning they cannot process, and secondary traumatization follows. What patients don't say when a family member is listening A mistranslation distorts what gets said. A family member in the room changes what gets said at all. Some subjects go quiet the moment a relative is holding the conversation: Domestic violence, especially when the interpreter is the person being asked about Substance use and alcohol Sexual history and reproductive health Mental health symptoms and suicidal thoughts Financial stress and housing instability A professional interpreter is bound by confidentiality and stays neutral. A relative is part of the relationship. Parents shield children from hard truths, and children soften bad news to spare a parent, so the fullest picture never reaches you. The history you build is only as accurate as the room allows. The legal line: what Section 1557 actually prohibits Everything above carries legal weight. Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act, through its 2024 final rule effective July 5, 2024, bars covered entities from relying on a minor child to interpret except as a temporary measure during an emergency involving an imminent threat to safety when no qualified interpreter is available. It also prohibits leaning on any unqualified adult companion. A qualified interpreter must: Be proficient in both languages Interpret effectively and impartially Know specialized medical vocabulary Follow interpreter ethics principles Any organization accepting Medicare, Medicaid, or federal funding is a covered entity. Fall short and you face Office for Civil Rights enforcement , litigation, and possible loss of funding. When a family member can appropriately assist The rule leaves room, though the openings are narrow. Two exceptions hold under the 2024 rule: A genuine emergency with an imminent safety threat and no qualified interpreter immediately reachable A patient with limited English proficiency who directly asks for a known adult to assist, where a qualified interpreter is present to confirm the request and the circumstances make relying on that adult reasonable Both are exceptions, not defaults. There is also a distinction worth holding onto. A relative sitting beside a patient for comfort is welcome. A relative carrying the clinical conversation is a different matter. Honor the first freely. Do not let it slide into the second. What qualified medical interpretation actually requires A relative who happens to speak two languages meets none of the standard that trained interpretation sets. Being qualified is a defined skill set, and the 2024 Section 1557 rule wrote that definition down precisely because self-reported bilingual ability kept getting used as the benchmark. A qualified medical interpreter brings: Command of medical terminology in both languages, from dosage units to diagnoses A code of ethics governing impartiality and role boundaries Complete transmission of what is said, without omitting, adding, or editorializing Binding confidentiality that a family member cannot offer Cultural competency that carries meaning, beyond words alone The error data points the same direction. Research on interpreter quality suggests trained interpreters produce fewer consequential errors than untrained ones. Scalable alternatives to ad hoc interpretation No single modality covers every encounter. A tiered program does. Modality Speed Language coverage After-hours Workflow fit Cost On-site staff interpreters Slow to schedule Narrow Limited Strong in person High Telephone interpretation Moderate Broad Usually available Audio only Per-minute Video remote interpretation Moderate Moderate Variable Needs device and bandwidth Per-minute AI medical interpretation Instant 150-plus languages 24/7 Integrates with EHR and telehealth Lower per-minute For routine and lower-acuity visits, AI medical interpretation vs. phone interpreter services is worth reviewing, and AI is the strong default given instant access at scale. Reserve qualified human interpreters for high-stakes moments where judgment and nuance matter most: complex informed consent, end-of-life conversations, and acute psychiatric crises. Build the escalation rules first, then match the tool to the encounter. How Opalite Health closes the ad hoc interpretation gap The workaround exists because access has been slow. Opalite Health closes that gap. Our AI interpreter for healthcare is built for clinical encounters and available instantly across more than 150 languages and dialects without scheduling delays or charges for silent minutes. It has been assessed in an independent validation study with Johns Hopkins Medicine, which found more than 90% fewer major and critical errors compared with certified medical interpreters. Every encounter runs through Opalite Guardian, our multi-layered quality and safety framework designed to detect and reduce clinically meaningful interpretation errors. Deploy Opalite on a risk-based framework: first-line interpretation for routine visits, with escalation to qualified human interpreters for the high-stakes situations your clinical and compliance policies define, as part of a broader strategy for closing healthcare language gaps . Integrations cover Epic, Cerner, eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, MEDITECH, and other leading EHRs. No child should have to relay a diagnosis. There is a structured, validated alternative. Moving beyond family members as medical interpreters Every encounter where an untrained family member holds the conversation is a gap in your clinical record and a potential Section 1557 exposure. See AI medical interpretation in action .

summary: WATERTOWN, Mass., Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- C4 Therapeutics, Inc. (C4T) (Nasdaq: CCCC), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to advancing targeted protein degradation science, today announced that the independent directors serving on the Organization, Leadership and
body_text: WATERTOWN, Mass., Aug. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- C4 Therapeutics, Inc. (C4T) (Nasdaq: CCCC), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to advancing targeted protein degradation science, today announced that the independent directors serving on the Organization, Leadership and Compensation Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors approved the grant of non-qualified stock options to purchase 162,880 shares of the Company’s common stock to one new employee (the “Inducement Grant”), with the grant made on August 10, 2026 (the “Grant Date”). The Inducement Grant was granted as a material inducement to this individual entering employment with C4T in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The Inducement Grant has an exercise price per share that is equal to the closing price of C4T’s common stock on the Grant Date. The Inducement Grant will vest over a four-year period, with 25% of the shares vesting on the first-year anniversary of the employee’s start date, with the remainder of the shares vesting in thirty-six equal monthly installments thereafter, subject to the employee’s continued employment with C4T through each vesting date. About C4 Therapeutics C4 Therapeutics (C4T) (Nasdaq: CCCC) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to delivering on the promise of targeted protein degradation science to create a new generation of medicines that transforms patients’ lives. C4T is progressing targeted oncology programs through clinical studies and leveraging its TORPEDO® platform to efficiently design and optimize small-molecule medicines to address difficult-to-treat diseases. C4T’s degrader medicines are designed to harness the body’s natural protein recycling system to rapidly degrade disease-causing proteins, offering the potential to overcome drug resistance, drug undruggable targets and improve patient outcomes. For more information, please visit www.c4therapeutics.com . body_text: Press Release Toolkit Subscribe RSS Feeds Contact IR Presentations Press Release Barinthus Bio Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Updates on Corporate Developments Aug 6, 2026 PDF Version Proposed combination with Clywedog Therapeutics Inc. (“Clywedog”) progressing towards closing Completed enrollment of 42 planned subjects in the Phase 1 AVALON trial evaluating VTP-1000 in patients with celiac disease; topline data from multiple ascending dose ("MAD") expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 GERMANTOWN, Md., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Barinthus Biotherapeutics plc (NASDAQ: BRNS) (“Barinthus Bio,” or the “Company”), today announced its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided an overview of the Company’s corporate developments. Barinthus Bio is an immunology and inflammation (“I&I”) company focused on developing therapies that promote immune tolerance with curative potential. “During the second quarter, our primary focus remained advancing the proposed combination with Clywedog and progressing the clinical development of VTP-1000, our lead asset for celiac disease,” said Bill Enright, Chief Executive Officer of Barinthus Bio. “We are pleased to announce the completion of enrollment in the multiple ascending dose portion of the Phase 1 AVALON trial and remain on track to report topline data in the fourth quarter of 2026. We believe VTP-1000 has the potential to address a significant unmet need in celiac disease and to be an important driver of long-term value for shareholders of the combined company.” Recent Corporate Developments During the third quarter of 2026, Barinthus Bio completed enrollment in all cohorts in the MAD portion of the Phase 1 AVALON clinical trial. On June 30, 2026, Barinthus Bio received a notice (the “Extension Notice”) from the Nasdaq Stock Market (“Nasdaq”) informing the Company that Nasdaq had granted the Company an additional 180 calendar days, or until December 28, 2026, to regain compliance with the Bid Price Requirement for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). In connection with the Extension Notice, the listing of the Company’s American Depositary Shares (the “ADSs”) was transferred from the Nasdaq Global Market to the Nasdaq Capital Market, effective as of July 2, 2026. The Extension Notice has no other immediate effect on the listing of the ADSs. Upcoming Milestones Celiac Disease (VTP-1000): Data from the MAD portion of the Phase 1 AVALON clinical trial, which includes a gluten challenge following three doses of test medication, is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. An abstract outlining Phase 1 Single Ascending Dose data for VTP-1000 has been selected for poster presentation at the American College of Gastroenterology ("ACG") Annual Scientific Meeting, to be held October 9–14, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. The poster will be presented by Dr. Adam Bledsoe, from the Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology at Mayo Clinic. Corporate: Barinthus Bio expects to complete the merger with Clywedog in the second half of 2026 which will result in a differentiated biopharmaceutical company focusing on metabolic and autoimmune diseases with three potentially disease-modifying clinical stage therapies. At closing, the combined company will be renamed “Clywedog Therapeutics Holdings, Inc.” and is expected to trade on the NASDAQ under the new ticker symbol “CLYD.” The combined company's estimated cash runway is expected to extend through 2027, supported by existing cash and additional investments by OrbiMed and Torrey Pines Investments, LLC, both existing shareholders in Clywedog, and new investors. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights Cash: As at June 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash were $59.6 million, compared to $67.2 million as of March 31, 2026. The $7.6 million decrease was a result of the net cash used in operating activities of which $8.1 million was used for the development of the Company's pipeline and general corporate expenses, and a $0.5 million translational gain from the conversion of balances in pound sterling denominated entities to the United States dollar reporting currency. Based on standalone research and development plans, the Company expects its available resources to fund its operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements for at least the next 12 months from the date of issuance of the financial statements. Research and Development Expenses: Research and development expenses were $3.9 million in the second quarter of 2026 compared to $3.6 million for the first quarter of 2026. The increase was primarily attributable to an increase in VTP-1000 Celiac program cost in second quarter of 2026 offset by reduced activity in the Barinthus legacy asset clinical programs and the reduction in workforce. The quarter-on-quarter research and development expenses are outlined in the following table, with the expense primarily attributable to the continued progression of the Phase 1 AVALON clinical trial of VTP-1000 in celiac disease, and the reduced activity on legacy assets in infectious disease and oncology. It is anticipated that research and development expenses related to the Barinthus legacy assets in infectious disease and oncology will continue to decrease going forward as the clinical trials complete, and that research and development expenses related to the autoimmune program will continue at current levels or increase, as the clinical development continues. title: Hormel Foods Named to Forbes List of America’s Best Employers for Women 2026
summary: The post Hormel Foods Named to Forbes List of America’s Best Employers for Women 2026 appeared first on Hormel Foods .
body_text: Explore This Section Hormel Foods Named to Forbes List of America’s Best Employers for Women 2026 Tags Careers Awards & Recognition Share This Article August 4, 2026 Austin , Minn. Recognized with a No. 65 ranking for fostering opportunity, growth and advancement for women At Hormel Foods, we believe our people are our greatest strength. We are proud to be named one of America’s Best Employers for Women 2026 by Forbes and Statista Inc., a recognition that highlights our ongoing commitment to cultivating an inclusive workplace where women are valued, empowered, and equipped to succeed at every stage of their careers. The ranking is based on an independent survey of more than 146,000 women across the United States, with more than 4 million employer evaluations considered over three years. The final list includes just 700 companies nationwide. From development programs and mentorship to inclusive policies and benefits, Hormel Foods continually invests in helping women build meaningful and rewarding careers. We are honored to receive this distinction and remain committed to building a workplace where everyone can thrive. Learn more about the ranking and view the complete Forbes list here. How Hormel Foods Encourages and Empowers Women Employee Resource Group Hormel Foods encourages employee-led initiatives that help strengthen connection, professional growth and leadership skills. Among these efforts is our employee resource group, Women’s Insights Network, which encourages community and elevates diverse perspectives at all levels across the company. Work-Life Balance We recognize that employees perform their best when they can balance work and personal responsibilities. That’s why Hormel Foods offers competitive benefits, including generous paid time off and parental leave programs designed to help women during important life moments. We also promote their well-being through comprehensive mental health resources available through Spring Health. Employees and their eligible family members have access to coaching, counseling, therapy and other personalized resources to enhance mental, emotional and overall well-being throughout different life stages and career journeys. Child Care and Family Support Supporting women also means supporting their families. We invested in a near-site early childhood education center in Austin, Minnesota, that serves children from 1 month to 12 years. Operated by Bright Horizons and accredited by the National Association for the Education of Young Children, the center helps employees and community members access high-quality child care and educational opportunities for their children. We also provide access to fertility and family-building benefits through Progyny. The program offers personalized guidance for fertility treatment, adoption, surrogacy and other paths to parenthood, along with access to specialized providers and care coordination resources. These benefits help women navigate important family decisions with confidence and clarity. Leadership and Growth Opportunities Hormel Foods is committed to developing future leaders. Through leadership development programs and training, women can build skills and make an impact. The company continues to have strong female representation across leadership roles and a pipeline of emerging leaders poised for future success. Women can also participate in mentorship opportunities that accelerate professional growth, knowledge sharing and career advancement. Continuing Our Commitment This recognition from Forbes underscores our ongoing commitment to creating an inclusive, supportive workplace. We are proud of the progress we’ve made in helping women thrive through programs and benefits that promote connection and well-being, while providing family-focused resources, leadership development and opportunities for long-term career success. title: Cova vs Flowhub: 2026 Dispensary POS Comparison
summary: Cova vs Flowhub compared for 2026: compliance, inventory, the new native e-commerce on both platforms, delivery gaps, and what an all-in-one replaces.
body_text: Cova and Flowhub are two established dispensary POS systems, and operators comparing them are really comparing three things: how each handles compliance, how each runs day to day, and what's still missing from each stack. Both have now shipped native e-commerce (Cova in late 2022, Flowhub in July 2025), which retires the oldest knock on both. What's left to weigh is delivery, which neither fully offers, and what the newer e-commerce products actually add to the monthly bill. This guide compares Cova vs Flowhub feature by feature for 2026, then shows where an all-in-one platform like Meadow closes the gap. In This Post Why Your Dispensary Software Matters Key Features to Evaluate in Dispensary Software Cova Overview Flowhub Overview Comparing Cova and Flowhub The High Cost of Fragmented Systems Final Thoughts: Cova vs Flowhub Why Meadow Stands Out as a Better Alternative Common Questions Why Your Dispensary Software Matters A dispensary POS system is more than just a tool for sales. It ensures seamless inventory management , simplifies compliance , and enhances the customer experience by supporting features like online menus , loyalty programs , and delivery services . Choosing the wrong platform can lead to inefficiencies, compliance risks, and frustrated staff. In contrast, the right system empowers cannabis business owners and their teams to streamline operations, improve profitability, and scale effectively. For the full evaluation framework, see How to Choose a Cannabis Dispensary POS System . Key Features to Evaluate in Dispensary Software When comparing Cova and Flowhub, it's worth evaluating them on the areas where they actually differ: Compliance : How well does it ensure adherence to state regulations? Inventory : Are counts accurate? Does it sync in real time across all menus? E-Commerce : Is the online store native, what does it include, and what does it cost on top of the POS? Delivery Tools : Does it offer integrated delivery tools? User Experience : Is the software easy to use, navigate, and train staff? Cova Overview Cova, headquartered in Denver, CO, and Vancouver, BC, is a dispensary software provider serving cannabis businesses across Canada and the U.S. It offers tools for compliance, sales, inventory tracking, and API integrations. Since late 2022, Cova has also offered Cova eCommerce, a plug-and-play online store that syncs with the POS in real time. Delivery remains the gap: Cova has no native delivery tools, so delivery operators rely on external solutions. Cova's Key Features: Compliance Tools : Automated track and trace compliance reporting. Inventory Management : Real-time tracking and inventory count importing. E-Commerce : Cova eCommerce, a native plug-and-play online store, priced at $149/month as of the writing of this article (included on enterprise plans, per Cova's site). Payment Processing : Supports cashless transactions through Cova Pay. Point-of-Sale : Supports in-store and order-ahead transactions, but no support for delivery. Cova Strengths: Regulatory Compliance : Tools to simplify adherence to state regulations. Inventory Management : Real-time inventory updates. Third-Party Integrations : Integrates with systems like Weedmaps, Leafly, and Alpine IQ. Cova Weaknesses: No Delivery Tools : Delivery services rely entirely on external solutions. E-Commerce Costs Extra and Keeps It Simple : Cova eCommerce is a separate monthly subscription (unless you're on an enterprise plan) and uses standardized layouts; Cova points retailers who need design freedom to third-party e-commerce partners instead. Issues with Speed & Reliability : Some users report long lag times and system crashes. Flowhub Overview Flowhub, founded in 2015, is another dispensary software platform focused on sales, compliance, and operations. Its mobile handheld scanner can be used for inventory management and customer check-in and verification. It also offers mobile analytics insights for quick anywhere access. In July 2025, Flowhub launched a POS-native e-commerce product with live inventory sync, a pricing and discount engine that matches the POS, and ACH pre-payment for online orders. Delivery tools remain limited, and several back-of-house workflows still lean on manual processes. Flowhub's Key Features: Nug : Handheld scanning for check-in and inventory management. E-Commerce : POS-native online ordering (launched July 2025) with live inventory sync and ACH pre-payment. Dispensary Analytics : Basic analytics dashboards available on mobile. Payment Processing : Cashless transactions with Flowhub Pay. Point-of-Sale : Supports in-store and order ahead transactions, with limited support for delivery. Flowhub Strengths: Mobile Scanning : Handheld mobile scanning for inventory and customer intake. User Interface : Clean UI that's easy to learn. Mobile Analytics : View analytics dashboards on mobile devices. Flowhub Weaknesses: E-Commerce Is Young : The native online store launched in July 2025, so it has a short track record; feature depth and integrations are still building out. Limited Delivery Tools : Delivery features are basic and don't include geofencing or automation. Manual Processes : Reporting, inventory reconciliation, and other tasks can be time-intensive and prone to errors. Comparing Cova and Flowhub Here is how the two platforms handle the five jobs above, with Meadow as the all-in-one reference point in each. Each section leads with the practical difference, then the detail. E-Commerce Both platforms now offer native e-commerce; the difference is what it costs and how proven it is. Cova : Cova eCommerce is native and syncs with the POS in real time, but it's a separate $149/month subscription (included on enterprise plans) with standardized layouts; Cova directs retailers who need advanced customization to third-party platforms, and many operators still run marketplace menus like Weedmaps or Leafly alongside it. Flowhub : Launched POS-native e-commerce in July 2025 with live inventory sync and ACH pre-payment. It's the newest piece of Flowhub's stack, so expect a shorter track record and a maturing feature set. Meadow : Built-in e-commerce with customizable online menus, included in the flat platform fee rather than sold as an add-on. Delivery Management Delivery is where the two platforms fall furthest behind, and where Meadow's advantage is most concrete. Cova : Does not support delivery. Operators must rely entirely on third-party software, which can be costly and inefficient. Flowhub : Provides limited delivery tools, with no support for dynamic delivery (e.g., Ice Cream Truck delivery model ) or advanced features like route optimization and geofencing. Meadow : Native hub-and-spoke and ice cream truck (dynamic) delivery with geofencing, automated dispatch, and real-time ledger compliance, no separate delivery vendor required.
