title: AI tutoring for kids: what parents need to know before the 2026-27 school year
summary: A parent's guide to AI tutoring tools for kids: what they do well, where they fall short, and when live human tutoring is the better choice for the 2026-27 school year.
body_text: A year ago, most parents hadn't heard of AI tutoring. Now it's a line item in Deloitte's 2026 back-to-school survey, alongside backpacks and school supplies [2]. The tools have arrived fast: Khanmigo, Duolingo Max, Photomath, and a growing roster of apps that promise personalized instruction at a fraction of the cost of a human tutor. Some of these tools deliver real value. Others over-promise. And for parents trying to figure out whether AI tutoring belongs in their kid's learning plan this fall, the landscape is hard to navigate without a clear look at what these tools can and can't do. This guide breaks down what AI tutoring looks like in practice, where the research says it helps, and where live, human instruction still has an edge that no algorithm can match. What AI tutoring looks like right now AI tutoring tools fall into a few broad categories, and knowing the differences matters when you're evaluating which (if any) might work for your kid. Practice-and-feedback engines like Khan Academy's Khanmigo and IXL's SmartScore adapt problem sets based on your kid's answers. Get a question wrong, and the system adjusts difficulty or offers a hint. These are strongest in math and grammar, where answers are clearly right or wrong and the path to understanding follows a predictable sequence. Conversational tutors powered by large language models can answer questions, explain concepts, and walk through problems step by step. Some are embedded in apps designed for kids; others are general-purpose chatbots that parents repurpose. The conversational format feels personal, but the quality of explanations varies widely, and younger kids can drift into off-topic exchanges without realizing it. Language learning apps like Duolingo Max use AI to simulate conversations in a target language. These work well for building vocabulary and basic fluency, though they can't replicate the cultural nuance and real-time correction of a live language class . Homework helpers like Photomath and Socratic let kids photograph a problem and get an instant solution with steps. Useful for checking work, but risky when kids use them to bypass the thinking process entirely. Where AI tutoring helps The Stanford Human-Centered AI Institute's 2025 review of AI in education found measurable gains in specific, narrow contexts [1]. AI tutoring tools tend to work best when: The subject has clear right-and-wrong answers. Math fact fluency, grammar rules, and vocabulary drills are well-suited to adaptive practice engines. The system knows when your kid gets it right and adjusts accordingly. Your kid needs repetition without judgment. Some kids freeze up when they get a math problem wrong in front of a teacher or parent. An AI tutor that adjusts and moves on can reduce that performance anxiety. You need a bridge between live sessions. For families using live one-on-one tutoring once or twice a week, an AI practice tool can keep skills sharp between sessions. Your kid is self-motivated and old enough to stay on task. The research suggests gains are strongest among older kids (ages 12 and up) who can use tools independently without constant redirection [1]. Where AI tutoring falls short The same research that highlights AI tutoring's strengths also reveals its limits. For parents, these limits matter more than the marketing copy suggests. It can't read the room. A human tutor notices when a kid's eyes glaze over, when frustration is building, when the real barrier isn't the math but something that happened at school that morning. AI tutors respond to inputs, not to the whole child. It struggles with open-ended thinking. Writing, critical analysis, scientific reasoning, historical interpretation: these subjects require a teacher who can push back on weak arguments, ask follow-up questions, and model the messy process of working through a problem. AI can generate a passable essay outline, but it can't teach your kid to develop their own voice or defend an idea under questioning. Research on screen time and learning reinforces that passive digital interactions don't produce the same cognitive gains as active, dialogic instruction. It doesn't build relationships. The Deloitte 2026 BTS survey found that a majority of parents considering AI tutoring still ranked "connection with a real teacher" as a top priority for their kid's learning [2]. Kids learn differently from someone who knows them, remembers what they struggled with last week, and celebrates genuine breakthroughs. Younger kids need more guardrails than most tools provide. For kids under 10, the attention management, comprehension checking, and redirection that a live teacher provides is hard to replicate. Most AI tutoring tools are designed for middle school and up, and younger kids often need a parent co-piloting the session to stay productive.

title: AI Cash Flow Forecasting: How It Works and Why It’s More Accurate
summary: AI cash flow forecasting uses machine learning to predict cash inflows and outflows from live data. Learn how it works, why it’s more accurate than spreadsheets, and how to start.
body_text: AI cash flow forecasting uses machine learning to predict a company’s future cash inflows and outflows, drawing on live data from banks, the ERP, billing, and other financial systems instead of a hand-built spreadsheet. It learns from historical patterns, refreshes continuously, and flags where cash is likely to run short or pile up, so finance can act before a problem becomes a crisis. Cash forecasting is the single most valuable thing a finance team does, and the hardest to get right. This guide explains what AI cash flow forecasting is, why traditional methods miss, how the AI approach works step by step, the benefits, and how to get started. What Is AI Cash Flow Forecasting? AI cash flow forecasting is the use of machine learning to project future cash inflows and outflows from live financial data. It connects to banks and ERPs, learns from historical cash patterns, and produces a continuously updated forecast, replacing the manual spreadsheet models treasurers traditionally built by hand. The difference from a normal forecast is not just automation. A spreadsheet forecast is a static snapshot built on assumptions a human typed in. An AI forecast is a living model that ingests new data, recognizes patterns a person would miss, and improves as it sees more actuals. Why Traditional Cash Forecasting Falls Short Treasury owns the most consequential question in finance, how much cash will we have and when , and most teams still answer it with tools that can’t keep up. Spreadsheets are still the default. 91% of treasury teams use Excel as one of their cash-forecasting tools, according to Strategic Treasurer’s Cash Forecasting & Visibility Survey reported by CTMfile . Spreadsheets don’t refresh bank feeds, don’t audit themselves, and break silently when a formula shifts. Accuracy is worse than most leaders assume. An EY-Parthenon analysis of roughly 2,400 of the largest global companies found only 28% of cash forecasts landed within 10% of actual free cash flow. When forecasts miss by that much, treasurers over-borrow, sit on idle cash, or get caught short. And it’s the hardest job on the desk. In the 2025 AFP Treasury Benchmarking Survey , based on more than 500 practitioners, over 60% named cash or liquidity forecasting their single most challenging task . The bottleneck is usually the data, which is fragmented across banks, entities, and systems, and stitched together by hand. For the mechanics of building a forecast the traditional way, see our guide to the direct vs. indirect cash flow methods . How AI Cash Flow Forecasting Works AI cash flow forecasting turns that manual process into a continuous, data-driven one. It generally works in five steps. 1. Connect and centralize the data The system connects directly to banks, the ERP, billing, and other financial systems, and pulls balances, transactions, invoices, and payment history into one place. This removes the manual export-and-paste step that makes spreadsheet forecasts stale on arrival. 2. Clean and categorize transactions The model classifies inflows and outflows, payroll, receivables, vendor payments, taxes, debt service, and learns the timing and seasonality of each. Consistent categorization is what lets the forecast reason about when cash actually moves, not just how much. 3. Learn patterns and predict Machine-learning models trained on historical cash behavior predict future inflows and outflows across horizons, from a daily 13-week view to longer-range planning. Because the model learns from every new actual, its predictions sharpen over time rather than drifting like a static spreadsheet. 4. Run scenarios and stress tests AI can generate many scenarios, such as a slow-paying customer, an FX swing, or a delayed raise, and show the cash impact of each. As J.P. Morgan notes , AI “generates thousands” of scenarios based on historical data and market conditions, far beyond a handful of hand-built cases. 5. Deliver and act The forecast lands where finance already works, in Slack, email, or a spreadsheet, with variances flagged and explained. The best systems don’t just show the number; they recommend or take the next action, like flagging a shortfall or drafting a sweep. This is closely related to how AI handles flux and variance analysis . Why AI Forecasts Are More Accurate The accuracy gains are real and well documented. According to J.P. Morgan , “AI-powered forecasting models can reduce error rates by up to 50% compared to traditional methods, according to case studies from multinational corporations.” Order-to-cash specialist HighRadius advertises up to 95% forecasting accuracy on high-volume receivables data. Three things drive the improvement: Live data instead of stale exports. The forecast reflects today’s balances and transactions, not last week’s spreadsheet. Pattern recognition beyond human capacity. Models catch timing and seasonality across thousands of data points that a person building a model by hand would miss. Continuous learning. Every actual that comes in tunes the next forecast, so accuracy compounds instead of decaying. One caveat matters: an AI forecast is only as good as the data feeding it. Fragmented or unreliable bank and ERP data is the top reason forecasts miss, so connectivity and data quality are prerequisites, not afterthoughts. Traditional vs. AI Cash Flow Forecasting Dimension Traditional (spreadsheet) AI cash flow forecasting Data Manual exports, stale on arrival Live feeds from banks and ERP Method Fixed assumptions typed by hand ML models that learn from actuals Refresh Rebuilt periodically Continuous, self-updating Scenarios A few hand-built cases Thousands, generated automatically Accuracy Often outside 10% of actual Up to 50% lower error (per J.P. Morgan) Effort Hours of manual work Automated, with humans reviewing Who Benefits Most From AI Cash Flow Forecasting The value shows up wherever cash timing is complex or the stakes are high. Corporate treasury teams get a real-time cash position and a rolling forecast instead of a once-a-day, manually assembled snapshot, freeing time for funding and risk decisions. See how this fits the broader corporate treasury function . FP&A and finance leaders get forecasts they can defend to a board, tied to drivers and updated continuously, which sharpens working capital management and planning. Lean and mid-market teams get enterprise-grade forecasting without an army of analysts, because the model does the pattern-finding that used to take a dedicated treasury desk. How to Get Started With AI Cash Flow Forecasting You don’t need to rip out your systems to adopt AI forecasting. A practical path: Consolidate your data first. Connect banks, ERP, and billing so the model has clean, complete inputs. Accuracy starts here. Pick a starting horizon. A daily or 13-week forecast is the highest-value place to begin for most treasury teams. Choose the right tool. Some platforms bolt AI onto a traditional TMS; others are AI-native. Compare the market in our best treasury management software guide, and see what a treasury management system does versus an AI-agent layer. Keep a human in the loop. Let the model do the forecasting and flag exceptions, while treasury reviews and owns the decisions. Concourse builds AI agents that connect directly to your ERP, data warehouse, billing, and banking data to run cash forecasting, variance analysis, AR and collections, and liquidity reporting end to end, with every number traceable back to source. More than 100 finance departments use Concourse to cut manual work by roughly 75% and save 20+ hours per person each month , and the platform is SOC 2 Type II certified, with data encrypted in transit and at rest. For treasury-specific workflows, read AI Agents for Treasury . Frequently Asked Questions What is AI cash flow forecasting? AI cash flow forecasting is the use of machine learning to predict future cash inflows and outflows from live financial data. It connects to banks and ERPs, learns from historical cash patterns, and produces a continuously updated forecast, replacing manual spreadsheet models. How accurate is AI cash flow forecasting? It is materially more accurate than manual methods. J.P. Morgan reports AI models can reduce forecast error rates by up to 50% versus traditional approaches, and vendors like HighRadius advertise up to 95% accuracy on high-volume data. Accuracy depends heavily on the quality and completeness of the bank and ERP data feeding the model. Can AI replace a treasury or FP&A analyst? No. AI automates the data gathering, modeling, and first-pass forecasting, but a human still reviews the output, sets policy, and owns the decision. The pattern most teams adopt is AI doing the work and flagging exceptions, with finance in the loop. What data does AI cash flow forecasting need? It needs historical and live transaction data, typically bank balances and transactions, ERP data, receivables and payables, and payment history. The more complete and clean the data, the more accurate the forecast, which is why data connectivity is the first step. Do I need to replace my TMS to use AI forecasting? Not necessarily. Some AI forecasting runs as an execution and analysis layer on top of your existing systems, while others are built into a TMS. If you rely on a TMS for bank connectivity and payments, an AI-agent layer like Concourse can run forecasting and analysis alongside it. The Bottom Line Cash forecasting has outgrown the spreadsheet. With only about a quarter of forecasts landing within 10% of actual and forecasting rated the hardest job on the treasury desk, the teams that win connect live data, forecast with AI, and keep a human on the decisions. If cash forecasting still means a manual spreadsheet that’s stale the moment it’s finished, AI agents can give you a continuous, traceable forecast instead. title: Dissecting the Credit Gap Amongst Filipinos: Why the Gap Isn't Just About Loan Access
summary: For a small business, access to credit is often treated as a yes-or-no question: can the business qualify for a loan? The question is certainly black or white. body_text: For a small business, access to credit is often treated as a yes-or-no question: can the business qualify for a loan? The question is certainly black or white. But what most miss is that businesses don't stay the same size after gaining access to a loan. A business may start by borrowing to restock inventory or cover a short-term cash gap. As it grows, its needs can change. It may need more working capital, a larger facility, or financing at a different point in its operating cycle. So, what if access to credit could evolve with the business, too? Data from loans given by our lending partners through the PayMongo platform offers an early view into what that can look like. Between January to July 2024 and January to July 2026, the average loan originated through the PayMongo platform nearly quadrupled, from ₱242,000 to ₱946,000. Over the same period, the number of loans disbursed grew 60%, while total capital deployed grew 524%. In other words, lending grew much more through larger loans than through more loans. PHP 242,000 → PHP 946,000 Average loan size taken by a merchant, January to July 2024 compared with January to July 2026 This matters in a country where access to finance remains a constraint on SME growth. The World Bank has identified access to finance as a barrier for Philippine businesses , while the ADB estimates that MSME loans account for just 3.9% of total Philippine bank lending and 2.1% of GDP. But the question isn't simply whether businesses can get credit. It's whether the financial system can respond as their needs and financial track record change. For merchants on PayMongo, lending partners can use transaction history built through the platform as part of their underwriting. PayMongo facilitates the credit experience; lending partners provide the financing. We compared matched periods across 2024, 2025 and 2026 to limit the effects of seasonality and incomplete-year comparisons. Learn More About PayMongo Capital Loan sizes are getting bigger The lending data shows that the amount of capital being accessed is changing. As mentioned, capital deployed grew 524%, compared with 60% growth in loan count, while the average amount per loan increased from ₱242,000 to ₱946,000. Part of that change reflects the fact that the products themselves have evolved. The Product Ceiling Moved PayMongo Capital launched in November 2023 with lending partners offering loans capped at ₱500,000. Our lending partners now offer term loans of up to ₱3 million and a revolving line of up to ₱10 million. The ceiling therefore rose at least sixfold across the comparison window, more than the 3.9x increase in average loan size.Put differently, merchants are borrowing larger amounts while filling a smaller proportion of the available maximum. This means the increase in average loan size partly reflects larger facilities becoming available, rather than merchants borrowing more against an unchanged product. This also suggests that when larger amounts of credit become available, there is demand for them. Repeat borrowing is another part of the picture Roughly one in five merchants who complete a loan takes another within six months. That shows that borrowing is not always a one-time event. While higher loan amounts suggest that merchants are willing to access more capital when it is available, repeat borrowing suggests that flexible terms and continued loan eligibility can encourage merchants to access capital again as their needs change. Higher acceptance Between 2025 and 2026, our lending partners extended fewer credit offers while a higher share of those offers were accepted. Offers fell about 10%, while the acceptance rate rose by roughly 58% on a relative basis. This suggests that increasing the number of offers was not, by itself, enough to increase borrowing. Reaching merchants who are more likely to need credit may matter as much as the number of offers extended. This may also suggest that the growing merchant base is becoming more receptive to borrowing, as credit offers are increasingly directed toward merchants who are more likely to need it. What this suggests about the Credit Gap The data points to a different way of thinking about the credit gap. Access to credit does not have to be a one-time assessment. It can evolve as a business builds a financial track record. Transaction-based underwriting uses a business's ongoing activity to inform credit decisions. As merchants build more transaction history, lenders can potentially develop a clearer picture of how the business operates and how much financing it may need. That can work in both directions. For businesses, it can create a path to credit based on their operating activity rather than relying solely on collateral or information fixed at the time of application. For lenders, it provides a more current view of the businesses they are assessing. The data we see on PayMongo is consistent with that model: merchants are accessing larger loans, acceptance is increasing even as the number of offers falls, and some merchants return for additional credit. The opportunity is not just to make more credit available. It is also to make credit more responsive to the businesses using it. A small business does not necessarily remain a small borrower. The next question is whether individual businesses actually graduate into larger amounts of credit as they build a longer transaction history. Sign Up As a PayMongo Merchant Methodology: Figures compare matched January to July periods for 2024, 2025 and 2026, covering merchants transacting on the PayMongo platform. Loan-size figures are blended across lending products. Repayment performance is deliberately excluded from this analysis: loans disbursed in 2026 have not had time to mature, and any year-on-year repayment comparison would measure loan age rather than borrower behaviour.

title: Rehearsal Dinner Planning Guide: Everything You Need to Know (2026)
summary: Rehearsal dinner planning typically begins 3 to 6 months before the wedding. The event follows the ceremony rehearsal (usually the night before the
body_text: Last Updated on August 5, 2026 by Joy Editors Rehearsal dinner planning typically begins 3 to 6 months before the wedding. The event follows the ceremony rehearsal (usually the night before the wedding) and includes the wedding party, immediate family, the officiant, and often out-of-town guests. Average costs range from $1,500 for a casual backyard dinner to $15,000 or more for a formal venue. The groom’s family traditionally hosts, though many modern couples now share expenses or self-fund the evening. What Is a Rehearsal Dinner? A rehearsal dinner is a gathering held after the wedding ceremony rehearsal, typically the evening before the wedding. It serves as a thank-you to the wedding party, a chance for both families to mingle, and a more intimate celebration before the big day. Traditionally, the event follows a run-through of the ceremony at the venue. The wedding party practices the processional, recessional, and cue timing with the officiant, then heads to dinner together. The meal can range from a casual backyard barbecue to a multi-course seated dinner at an upscale restaurant. In recent years, rehearsal dinners have evolved beyond a simple post-rehearsal meal. Many couples now treat the evening as a meaningful event in its own right, complete with personalized decor, toasts, slideshows, and activities that set the tone for the wedding weekend. Who Plans and Pays for the Rehearsal Dinner? By long-standing tradition, the groom’s parents host and pay for the rehearsal dinner. This custom dates back to when the bride’s family covered the wedding reception, and the groom’s family took responsibility for the pre-wedding gathering. Modern approaches vary widely. Here are the most common arrangements: Groom’s parents host: They choose the venue, handle the budget, and coordinate logistics. This remains the most common arrangement. Shared hosting: Both sets of parents split costs and planning duties, which is increasingly popular when families live in different cities. Couple self-funds: Many couples in their late 20s and 30s prefer to plan and pay for the event themselves, keeping full control over style and guest list. Bride’s parents host: In some cultural traditions or family situations, the bride’s parents take the lead. No matter the arrangement, start the budget conversation early. A direct, respectful discussion 6 months before the wedding prevents misunderstandings. Frame it simply: “We are starting to plan the rehearsal dinner. Would you like to be involved, and if so, how?” For a deeper look at traditional and modern payment norms, search for detailed guides on “who pays for rehearsal dinner” etiquette. Editor’s Tip: In our experience, the smoothest budget conversations happen when the couple proposes a specific number first, rather than asking open-ended questions. Come prepared with a ballpark figure and two or three venue options at different price points. It turns a potentially awkward talk into a practical planning session, and it signals to parents that you have done your homework. Rehearsal Dinner Planning Timeline Use this month-by-month checklist to stay on track. Starting 4 to 6 months out gives plenty of buffer for popular venues and catering bookings. 4 to 6 Months Before the Wedding Confirm who is hosting and establish the budget range Set the date (almost always the night before the wedding) Coordinate with your officiant and venue on rehearsal time (typically 5:00 to 6:00 p.m.) Draft a preliminary guest list Begin researching venues near the ceremony or reception site 3 to 4 Months Before Book the venue or reserve the space (restaurants, private dining rooms, and event spaces fill quickly for Friday evenings) Choose a catering style: plated dinner, buffet, family-style, or food trucks Send save-the-date communication to out-of-town guests so they can plan travel Decide on a theme or dress code that complements (but does not upstage) the wedding 6 to 8 Weeks Before Send formal invitations (paper or digital) with venue address, start time, dress code, and parking details Finalize the guest list and collect RSVPs Confirm menu selections and communicate dietary restrictions to the caterer Plan any toasts, slideshows, or activities Order or plan decor (centerpieces, signage, photo displays) 2 to 3 Weeks Before Confirm final headcount with the venue or caterer Create a seating chart (if applicable) that mixes families and friend groups Brief toast-givers on time limits (3 minutes per person, 4 to 5 speakers maximum) Prepare any gifts for the wedding party Arrange transportation between the rehearsal site and dinner venue if they are in different locations 1 Week Before Send a detailed schedule to the wedding party with arrival times, addresses, and parking instructions Confirm all vendor details (flowers, AV equipment, musician or playlist) Prepare a printed or digital run-of-show for the host and any speakers Check weather forecasts if the event is outdoors and activate your backup plan if needed Day Of Arrive at the rehearsal venue 15 to 20 minutes early Run through the ceremony (processional order, cue timing, readings, recessional) Travel to the dinner venue (allow 20 to 40 minutes for transit) Enjoy dinner, toasts, and quality time with your closest people Wrap up by 9:30 to 10:00 p.m. so the couple gets enough rest before the wedding How to Set Your Rehearsal Dinner Budget One of the biggest gaps in rehearsal dinner planning is specific budget guidance. Costs vary enormously depending on your guest count, location, and style. Use these tiers as a starting point: Style Guest Count Estimated Total Cost Per-Person Range Casual (backyard BBQ, pizza party, taco bar) 20 to 30 $1,500 to $3,000 $50 to $100 Mid-range (restaurant private dining, buffet catering) 30 to 50 $3,000 to $8,000 $75 to $160 Upscale (fine dining, full bar, plated multi-course) 40 to 75 $8,000 to $15,000+ $150 to $250+ Budget Breakdown by Category Here is how costs typically distribute across major categories: Venue rental: 0 to 25% (many restaurants waive fees with a food minimum; private homes cost nothing) Food and catering: 40 to 50% (the largest expense regardless of style) Drinks and bar service: 15 to 25% (open bar costs more; consider a limited cocktail menu or BYOB venue) Decor and flowers: 5 to 10% (keep it simple since the wedding is tomorrow) Invitations: 2 to 5% (digital invitations reduce this to nearly zero) Entertainment and extras: 5 to 10% (slideshow, games, welcome gifts) Money-Saving Tips Choose a restaurant with a private room instead of renting a separate event space. Many waive the room fee when you meet a food and beverage minimum. Host on a Thursday evening instead of Friday if your schedule allows. Venue and catering rates drop significantly on weeknights. Opt for family-style or buffet service, which costs 20 to 30% less than plated meals. Use digital invitations and a free online RSVP system to eliminate printing and postage costs. Skip elaborate floral arrangements. Simple candles, greenery, and photo displays create warmth without the expense. Rehearsal Dinner Budget Calculator Rehearsal Dinner Budget Calculator Adjust the inputs below to get a personalized cost estimate based on real rehearsal dinner pricing data. Guest Count Dinner Style Open Bar? Venue Type Estimated Total $4,250 Estimated Breakdown Food and Catering $1,910 Drinks and Bar $940 Venue Rental $210 Decor and Flowers $340 Invitations $130 Entertainment and Extras $300 Contingency $210 Building Your Guest List The rehearsal dinner guest list is more selective than the wedding itself. Start with the essential core group, then expand based on budget and preference. Core Guest List (Always Invited) The couple Parents and stepparents of the couple Siblings (and their partners) Grandparents All members of the wedding party (bridesmaids, groomsmen, flower children, ring bearers) and their partners The officiant (and their partner) Wedding planner or coordinator (optional, but a nice gesture) Extended Guest List (Budget Permitting) Out-of-town guests who traveled for the wedding Close aunts, uncles, and cousins not in the wedding party Parents’ close friends (especially if parents are hosting) Readers, musicians, or other ceremony participants A common point of etiquette: if you invite out-of-town guests, invite all of them. Selectively including only some can create awkwardness. For a complete breakdown of who to include (and how to handle edge cases), read the full rehearsal dinner guest list guide . Pro Tip: A dedicated guest list manager lets you tag rehearsal dinner invitees separately from the full wedding list. This makes it easy to send targeted communications, track RSVPs for the rehearsal dinner only, and avoid accidentally leaving someone out. Being able to filter by event saves real headaches when you are juggling multiple gatherings across a wedding weekend. Choosing the Right Venue The venue sets the tone for the entire evening. Choose a space that reflects your style, accommodates your guest count comfortably, and works logistically with your rehearsal location. Venue Types Compared Venue Type Best For Typical Cost Key Considerations Restaurant private dining room Groups of 20 to 50 $$ to $$$ Often no rental fee with food minimum; limited decor flexibility Backyard or private home Any size; casual vibe $ to $$ Full control over decor and schedule; requires more DIY coordination Event space or banquet hall Large groups (50+) $$$ to $$$$ Maximum flexibility; typically requires outside catering Brewery, winery, or rooftop Groups of 20 to 60 $$ to $$$ Built-in ambiance; may have noise or weather constraints Hotel meeting room or ballroom Destination weddings; large groups $$$ to $$$$ Convenient if guests are staying at the hotel; in-house catering required Questions to Ask Every Venue What is the minimum and maximum guest capacity for the space? Is there a room rental fee, or do you waive it with a food and beverage minimum? Can we bring our own decor, music, or AV equipment? What is the cancellation or change policy? Is there dedicated parking, and is it free? Do you offer a rain backup if the space is outdoors? Editor’s Tip: Visit your top venue choices on the same day of the week and time of evening as your rehearsal dinner. A restaurant that feels spacious on a Tuesday afternoon can be packed and deafening on a Friday at 7 p.m. Pay attention to noise levels, lighting (will it feel warm enough for toasts?), and whether staff seem attentive during the rush. Those details matter more than the decor in photos. Destination Wedding Considerations For destination weddings, the rehearsal dinner often doubles as a welcome event for guests arriving from out of town. Keep these logistics in mind: Book a venue within walking distance of the hotel block to simplify transportation. If you have negotiated group hotel rates , choose a dinner spot that your guests can reach on foot. Consider a welcome cocktail party format instead of a formal seated dinner, which accommodates guests arriving at different times. Share detailed directions, parking, and dress code information in advance. A wedding website with dedicated event pages keeps the full schedule, venue maps, and hotel block details in one place so guests can reference everything on their phones. Menu Planning and Dietary Accommodations The food is often what guests remember most about the rehearsal dinner. Match the menu to the tone of the evening, and plan for dietary needs well in advance. Menu Styles by Formality Casual: BBQ, pizza, tacos, food trucks, or a potluck-style buffet. Great for outdoor or backyard settings. Budget-friendly and low-stress. Semi-formal: Buffet or family-style service at a restaurant. Allows variety while keeping costs moderate. Works well for groups of 30 to 60. Formal: Plated multi-course dinner with wine pairings. Best for smaller groups (under 40) at upscale restaurants or private dining rooms. Handling Dietary Restrictions Collect dietary information when you gather RSVPs. Common needs to plan for include: Vegetarian and vegan options (plan for at least one of each) Gluten-free alternatives Nut allergies and other serious food allergies Kosher or halal requirements Children’s portions or a kid-friendly menu option Pro Tip: Share the menu with the venue or caterer at least 2 weeks before the event. Most restaurants can accommodate special requests with advance notice but struggle with last-minute changes. Drink Service Options Open bar: Most generous but most expensive. Budget $30 to $60 per person for a 3-hour event. Limited cocktail menu: Offer 2 to 3 signature drinks plus beer and wine. Cuts bar costs by 30 to 40%. Wine and beer only: A refined but affordable option, especially if the venue charges high spirit markups. BYOB venue: Some restaurants and private spaces allow guests to bring their own alcohol. This can reduce drink costs to $10 to $15 per person (corkage fee only). Rehearsal Dinner Etiquette Good etiquette keeps everyone comfortable and sets a gracious tone for the wedding weekend. Here are the guidelines that matter most. Dress Code The rehearsal dinner should be one step less formal than the wedding reception. If the wedding is black tie, aim for cocktail attire at the rehearsal dinner. If the wedding is casual-elegant, go with smart casual. Always communicate the dress code clearly on the invitation. Invitation Timing and Wording Send rehearsal dinner invitations 6 to 8 weeks before the event. Some couples include a rehearsal dinner card in the main wedding invitation suite. Digital invitations work particularly well for this event: they allow easy RSVP tracking, let you send updates if details change, and keep your rehearsal dinner responses separate from your main wedding count. Keep the wording warm and straightforward. Include: Host names (“John and Mary Smith invite you to…”) Date, time, and location with address Dress code RSVP instructions and deadline Parking and transportation notes Gift-Giving at the Rehearsal Dinner The rehearsal dinner is the traditional time for the couple to give thank-you gifts to the wedding party. It is also common for hosts to present a small token to the couple. Gifts are not expected from guests attending the dinner. Modern Etiquette Updates Some traditional rules have relaxed in recent years: Old rule: Only the groom’s parents can host. Modern take: Anyone can host or co-host. Old rule: The rehearsal dinner must be a formal sit-down meal. Modern take: Cocktail parties, game nights, and casual cookouts all qualify. Old rule: The dinner must be the night before the wedding. Modern take: Two nights before works if the rehearsal is held earlier or if the couple wants a rest day. One rule that still holds: The rehearsal dinner should never be more lavish or more formal than the wedding reception itself. Keep it complementary, not competitive. Speeches and Toasts: Who Speaks and When Toasts are one of the most memorable parts of a rehearsal dinner. Unlike the wedding reception, the rehearsal dinner is the right setting for longer, more personal stories and remarks from family. Recommended Speaker Order Host (traditionally groom’s parent): Welcome guests, share a short story or sentiment about the couple Other parent(s): Brief remarks from the bride’s parents or other family members Maid of honor and/or best man: A preview or personal story (save the big speech for the reception) Other wedding party members or close friends: Optional, by invitation only The couple: Close with a thank-you to the hosts, wedding party, and guests Time Guidelines Aim for 4 to 5 speakers total, with each keeping remarks under 3 minutes. That puts total toast time at 12 to 15 minutes, which is enough to feel meaningful without cutting into dinner conversation. Brief the speakers in advance so they know their time slot and the overall order. Pro Tip: Schedule toasts during dessert or between courses rather than before the meal begins. Hungry guests are distracted guests. Editor’s Tip: Assign someone (not the couple) to record the toasts on a phone propped at a good angle. Rehearsal dinner speeches are often more heartfelt and unguarded than reception toasts, and couples consistently tell us they wish they had captured them. A simple tripod and a phone in video mode is all it takes. Day-of Timeline and Run of Show A clear timeline keeps the evening flowing smoothly. Here is a sample schedule based on a 5:00 p.m. ceremony rehearsal: Time Activity Notes 4:40 p.m. Wedding party arrives at ceremony venue Tell latecomers to arrive 30 minutes earlier than the actual start 5:00 p.m. Ceremony rehearsal begins Officiant leads run-through of processional, readings, vows, recessional 5:45 to 6:00 p.m. Rehearsal ends Typical rehearsal lasts 30 to 60 minutes 6:00 to 6:30 p.m. Travel to dinner venue Allow 20 to 40 minutes for transit; share address and parking info in advance 6:30 to 7:00 p.m. Cocktails and mingling Drinks and light appetizers while guests settle in 7:00 p.m. Dinner is served Host offers a brief welcome toast before the first course 8:00 to 8:30 p.m. Toasts and speeches 4 to 5 speakers, 3 minutes each, during or after dessert 8:30 to 9:00 p.m. Gifts and activities Wedding party gifts, slideshows, or lawn games if applicable 9:30 to 10:00 p.m. Evening wraps up Couple should aim for a reasonable bedtime before the wedding Pro Tip: If the rehearsal venue and dinner location are more than 20 minutes apart, consider arranging a shuttle or rideshare group. Guests unfamiliar with the area will appreciate not having to navigate on their own. Creative Themes and Ideas The rehearsal dinner is a chance to show a different side of your personality than the wedding itself. Here are ideas organized by formality: Casual and Fun Backyard BBQ with lawn games (cornhole, bocce, croquet) Pizza party at a local pizzeria with a private room Taco bar or food truck night at a park or private property Clambake or seafood boil (perfect for coastal weddings) Cooking class where guests prepare the meal together Elegant and Classic Private dining room at a favorite restaurant Wine or whiskey tasting dinner with paired courses Garden party with a seated dinner under a tent Rooftop dinner with city views Unique and Memorable Progressive dinner that moves between 2 to 3 nearby locations (appetizers, entrees, dessert) Boat cruise dinner on a lake or river Farm-to-table dinner at a local farm Game night with trivia about the couple, board games, and prizes Editor’s Tip: The best rehearsal dinner themes are not picked from a list. They grow from something specific to the couple. Think about where you had your first date, a shared hobby, or a trip that defined your relationship. A couple who bonded over hiking does not need a formal ballroom; a trailhead picnic with lanterns tells their story better than any Pinterest board could. Let the theme be a chapter of your life, not a production. For more inspiration, browse dozens of creative rehearsal dinner themes and ideas with photos and planning tips. Common Rehearsal Dinner Mistakes to Avoid Even well-organized hosts make these errors. Learn from them before they happen: Starting too late: Popular Friday-night restaurant spaces book 3 to 4 months ahead. Waiting until 6 weeks out limits options significantly. Outshining the wedding: A rehearsal dinner that is more elaborate, more expensive, or more formal than the reception creates awkward comparisons. Keep it complementary. Forgetting dietary needs: At least one guest will have a restriction. Ask about allergies and preferences when collecting RSVPs, not the week of the event. Not providing clear directions: Guests traveling from out of town need more than just an address. Include parking instructions, transit time from the rehearsal, and dress code details. Letting toasts run long: Without time limits, speeches can stretch past 45 minutes. Brief speakers in advance and designate someone to keep things moving. Keeping the couple up too late: A rehearsal dinner that turns into a late-night party leaves the couple exhausted for their wedding day. Aim for a 9:30 to 10:00 p.m. wrap-up. Inviting a partial out-of-town group: If you invite some out-of-town guests, invite all of them. Selective inclusion creates hurt feelings the day before the wedding. Managing Rehearsal Dinner Logistics with Digital Tools Coordinating a rehearsal dinner alongside the wedding itself creates real logistical challenges. You need to manage a separate guest list, track different RSVPs, communicate specific details to a subset of invitees, and keep everything organized without it bleeding into your wedding planning workflow. A wedding website with multi-event support solves most of these problems in one place. Here is what to look for in a planning tool: Separate event pages: Create a dedicated rehearsal dinner event with its own time, location, dress code, and description. Only invited guests see the details. Tagged guest lists: Tag rehearsal dinner invitees separately from the full wedding list so you can quickly view, sort, and message just that group. Independent RSVP tracking: Collect rehearsal dinner RSVPs through a dedicated RSVP system without mixing them into your wedding RSVP count. Track who has responded and who needs a follow-up. Group messaging: Send targeted updates (parking changes, dress code reminders, time adjustments) only to rehearsal dinner attendees without cluttering everyone else’s inbox. Multi-event weekend view: Guests see a personalized schedule showing only the events they are invited to, from the rehearsal dinner through the wedding to any post-wedding brunch. For hotel logistics specifically, setting up a hotel room block and linking it directly from your event pages saves guests the hassle of searching for accommodations on their own. Frequently Asked Questions What is the order of events at a rehearsal dinner? A typical rehearsal dinner follows this order: cocktails and mingling (30 minutes), a welcome toast from the host, dinner service (60 to 90 minutes), speeches and toasts during or after dessert (15 to 20 minutes), and then optional activities like gift-giving or a slideshow. The entire evening usually lasts 2.5 to 3.5 hours. Who is supposed to plan the rehearsal dinner? Traditionally, the groom’s parents plan and host the rehearsal dinner. However, modern weddings often see the couple themselves, both sets of parents together, or even close friends coordinating the event. The key is to have an early conversation about roles, budget, and expectations so everyone is aligned. What is a reasonable budget for a rehearsal dinner? Budget depends on guest count, location, and style. A casual backyard dinner for 20 guests might cost $1,500 to $3,000. A mid-range restaurant dinner for 40 guests typically runs $3,000 to $8,000. An upscale multi-course dinner for 50 or more guests can reach $8,000 to $15,000 or more. Food and drinks account for 55 to 75% of the total budget. How far in advance should you plan a rehearsal dinner? Start planning 4 to 6 months before the wedding. Book the venue 3 to 4 months out, send invitations 6 to 8 weeks ahead, and finalize the headcount and menu 2 to 3 weeks before the event. Popular Friday-evening restaurant spaces fill quickly, so earlier is better for venue booking. Do you have to invite out-of-town guests to the rehearsal dinner? It is not required, but it is a thoughtful gesture, especially if guests have traveled a long distance. The etiquette guideline is: if you invite some out-of-town guests, invite all of them. If your budget does not allow for a large group, consider hosting a separate, informal welcome gathering (drinks at a nearby bar, for example) for extended out-of-town guests.

title: Navier AI Awarded AFWERX Phase I SBIR to Build a Geometry Reasoning Layer for Engineering Agents
summary: Navier AI has been awarded a Phase I SBIR from AFWERX to explore an ontology-based geometry embedding layer that gives AI agents the ability to reason about parts, features, and spatial relationships instead of guessing.
body_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CA, August 18, 2026 - Navier AI, which is building the autonomous engineer for hardware design and development, today announced it has been awarded a Phase I Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) contract from AFWERX, the innovation arm of the Department of the Air Force. The award funds the exploration of an ontology-based geometry embedding layer for agentic spatial reasoning. Foundational model AI agents have proven to be capable at code and language. However, they remain weak at 3D. Ask an agent to reason about a bracket, a manifold, or a control surface, and it has no reliable way to know what it is looking at: which face is a mating surface, which feature is a fastener hole, what is upstream of what, or which part carries the load. Today's models see triangles and coordinates, not engineering intent. Under this Phase I effort, Navier AI is building the layer that enables agents to do spatial reasoning. "Agents have uneven performance across engineering problems. They're great at code, which actually makes them great for a lot of engineering work, but 3D and spatial reasoning remain large gaps. We're exploring the development of an agent ontology for 3D and spatial reasoning so agents can do more meaningful work in 3D. We see this as a fundamental layer of the autonomous hardware engineer." — Cameron Flannery, Founder and CEO of Navier AI About Navier AI Navier AI is building the autonomous engineer for hardware design and development. Its Agent-Driven Engineering (ADE) platform combines AI agents and compute infrastructure so engineering teams can automate simulation and analysis workflows. Navier AI's agents run physics simulations across aerospace, defense, automotive, and industrials. Learn more at navier.ai About AFWERX AFWERX is the innovation arm of the Department of the Air Force and a directorate within the Air Force Research Laboratory. It manages the Department of the Air Force SBIR/STTR program, connecting small businesses and non-traditional partners with Air Force and Space Force needs to accelerate the delivery of new technology. The views expressed are those of the author and do not reflect the official guidance or position of the United States Government, the Department of Defense, or the United States Air Force.

title: Signs your finance team is still manual, even with spreadsheets and systems
summary: Learn the main signs that finance still depends on manual work, even when the company uses an ERP, spreadsheets, and multiple systems.
body_text: Signs your finance team is still manual, even with spreadsheets and systems A finance team can have an ERP, organized spreadsheets, and integrated systems—and still be manual. The clearest signal is not the absence of technology, but the dependence on people to check, correct, decide, and explain every step. Having systems does not mean the finance process is automated. Many companies only realize how much they still depend on manual work when someone goes on vacation, resigns, or when transaction volume grows faster than the team. The same pattern appears in HR: leave management and PTO tracking tools such as actiPLANS help move requests, approvals, and balances out of spreadsheets. In finance, the challenge is similar: turning manual follow-up into a traceable workflow. A few signals help identify this before it becomes a larger problem. 1. Someone "knows" the process, but the system does not If you need to ask a specific person why a payment was approved or rejected, the process lives in someone's head, not in the system. This is a classic sign of a manual operation disguised as a structured process. The same happens when a rule exists only in messages, emails, side spreadsheets, or informal agreements. In an automated process, the rule is recorded in the workflow and can be reviewed later, including for audit purposes. 2. Month-end close depends on concentrated effort When the accounting or finance close requires the team to stop almost everything for three or four days to check postings, it usually means validation throughout the month is not automated. The work is simply being pushed to the end. Instead of checking data continuously, finance discovers discrepancies late, under deadline pressure and with less time to correct them. If this is a recurring bottleneck, read about automated finance close . 3. Excel is used as a bridge between systems Excel as an analysis tool is healthy. Excel as an integration layer between systems is a symptom. If someone needs to export a report from one system, adjust it in Excel, and import it into another, there is an automation gap. This creates version risk, formula errors, loss of traceability, and dependency on whoever knows how to use the "right spreadsheet." 4. Errors appear only after they cause problems Duplicate payments, divergent invoices, or out-of-policy postings identified only during audit or close indicate that checks are happening too late. Ideally, validation happens when data enters the process, not weeks later. For accounts payable, read the guide on how to avoid duplicate payments . 5. More volume means hiring more people to operate If doubling the number of invoices processed each month means doubling, or nearly doubling, the accounts payable team, the process is scaling manually. A well-automated process should absorb a relevant share of growth without a proportional increase in operational headcount. That does not mean the finance team stops growing. It means it grows in analysis, control, and decision-making—not only repetitive checking. 6. Process status depends on chat messages When someone needs to ask "has this invoice been approved?", "has this payment gone out?", or "who owns this pending item?", the workflow is not providing enough visibility. An automated process should show status, owner, blocking reason, and next action clearly. This is one reason to structure finance workflows with approval trails and exception handling. Checklist: signs of manual operation Signal What it indicates Rule in someone's head Low traceability Excel as a bridge Missing integration/automation Intense month-end close Late validation Error found after the fact Reactive control Headcount grows with volume Manual scaling Status by chat Missing workflow Why it is worth mapping this None of these signs, alone, is necessarily alarming. But when two or three appear together, they usually indicate that finance is spending qualified time and attention on checking and correction tasks that could run with automation. The benefit is not only speed. It is freeing the team for analysis, decision-making, negotiation, control, and continuous improvement—where finance truly adds value to the business. FAQ Does having an ERP mean finance is automated? No. The ERP structures data and records, but many processes remain manual when validation, approval, and exception handling depend on people. Are spreadsheets always a problem? No. Spreadsheets are useful for analysis. The problem is when they become the operational bridge between systems or the only source of process control. How should a team start mapping manual processes? Start with the areas that have the highest volume, rework, and risk: accounts payable, reconciliation, close, expense classification, and approvals. Conclusion Manual finance does not disappear when a company buys systems. It disappears when rules, validations, status, and exceptions stop depending on people's memory and daily checking. If the team still needs to ask, export, check, and correct everything manually, the process may be digital—but it is not yet automated.

title: Bioventus Reports Second Quarter Financial Results
summary: Q2 reported revenue of $153.2 million increased 4% Q2 GAAP earnings of $0.47 per diluted share compared to the prior-year period earnings of $0.11 per diluted share Non-GAAP earnings* of $0.22 per diluted share compared to $0.21 per diluted share in the prior-year period Cash from operations
body_text: News Release Details News Releases Events Presentations Bioventus Reports Second Quarter Financial Results August 5, 2026 PDF Version Q2 reported revenue of $153.2 million increased 4% Q2 GAAP earnings of $0.47 per diluted share compared to the prior-year period earnings of $0.11 per diluted share Non-GAAP earnings* of $0.22 per diluted share compared to $0.21 per diluted share in the prior-year period Cash from operations totaled $19.9 million Company reaffirms revenue, Adjusted Diluted EPS* and cash from operations guidance for the full year 2026 Company initiates review of strategic alternatives DURHAM, N.C., Aug. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Bioventus Inc. (Nasdaq: BVS) (“Bioventus” or the “Company”), a global leader in innovations for active healing, today reported financial results for the three and six months ended June 27, 2026. "Bioventus continued its positive momentum in the second quarter, with solid performance that positions us well for continued success in the second half of the year,” said Rob Claypoole, Bioventus President and Chief Executive Officer." We remain focused on disciplined execution while continuing to invest in our four growth drivers. We believe this compelling combination will accelerate revenue growth, strengthen profitability and earnings power, and drive significant free cash flow." “The Bioventus Board of Directors has full confidence in the business and management team and is excited about the future prospects of the Company,” Claypoole continued. “At the same time, in light of the external interest we have received, the Board has formed a committee of independent directors, which has determined it is the right time to initiate a review of strategic alternatives. This decision reflects our steadfast commitment to exploring all opportunities to maximize value for our shareholders.” Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results For the second quarter, worldwide revenue of $153.2 million advanced 4%, driven by double-digit growth in Pain Treatments.
